title: lazy canonical KV Mirror read
hypothesis: For logical K/V views related by known structured right-transforms K_m=K A_m and V_m=V B_m, one canonical physical cache can reproduce materialized-view attention exactly by transforming only the current query and attention output, eliminating prefix-length-dependent cache conversion on view switches.

runtime.interpretation: exploratory microbenchmark only; not a GPU or production claim

storage.authority: tensor numel * element_size for live KV state plus explicit View-code tensor bytes
storage.physical_aliasing_goal: one canonical K/V allocation regardless of logical View count

success_gate: All three fresh seeds satisfy every exactness gate at every tested prefix length; canonical cache storage is independent of logical View count except for View-code bytes; measured full-cache materialization cost increases with prefix length.
failure_gate: Any exactness gate fails on a fresh seed, or the claimed lazy computation requires a separate physical K/V cache per View.
boundaries: teacher/View relation is exact by construction
arbitrary earlier FFN changes are not assumed cache-transformable
